newsitem.title: CHINA: China says Dalai Lama "ganging up" with Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: China says Dalai Lama "ganging up" with Taiwan.

text.p: China on Friday accused Tibet's exiled Buddhist spiritual leader the Dalai Lama of "ganging up" with Taiwan in a plot to shatter China's territorial integrity.

The Dalai Lama has said he plans to visit Taiwan, an island the Chinese authorities regard as a rebel province, in March. Taiwan's mass-circulation United Daily News said the Dalai Lama could meet President Lee Teng-hui during his visit.

"The invitation to the Dalai Lama to visit Taiwan fully indicates the Taiwan authorities and the Dalai Lama are ganging up and using each other," the Xinhua news agency said, quoting a spokesman for the Taiwan Affairs Office of the State Council, or cabinet.
"The Taiwan authorities and the Dalai Lama...publicly engage in evil deeds and walk further and further away along the road of splitting the motherland," the spokesman said.
The Dalai Lama, who fled into exile in India after an anti-Chinese uprising in 1959, has said his visit to Taiwan is a purely spiritual event aimed at bringing Chinese and Tibetans closer together.
The spokesman vowed China would never allow plots to split the motherland to succeed.
Beijing and Taipei have been diplomatic rivals since the Communists defeated and drove the Nationalists into exile in Taiwan in 1949.
China conducted missile tests and war games near Taiwan in March 1996 in the run-up to the island's first direct presidential elections.
